headline: SpaceX says Starlink's call centres already use its Grok Voice AI to answer about 20,000 customer calls a day, with roughly 70 percent solved without a human.
score_reason: Pool score 5 lowered by 1: the Grok Voice 3.0 release was on 14 Oct 2026 and our 15 Oct edition already carried it with SpaceX's own usage claims; the figures remain the company's own.
importance_line: Starlink customers who phone for help will often reach an AI voice, and other companies may copy the model, but the figures are SpaceX's own and it did not say which languages or which calls still need a person.
summary: Business Insider reports that SpaceX, Elon Musk's combined space and AI company, said this week, as it announced a new Grok Voice model (Grok Voice 3.0 was released on 14 Oct 2026), that Starlink's call centres already use Grok Voice agents to handle about 20,000 customer calls a day, roughly 70 percent resolved without a human, with the agents verifying customers, troubleshooting hardware, issuing credits and shipping replacement equipment in several languages. These are SpaceX's own figures, and the company did not answer Business Insider's questions about which languages are supported or what calls still need a person.
notes: Read Business Insider in full. Follow-up of our 15 Oct entry on Grok Voice 3.0 (released 14 Oct 2026), which already flagged SpaceX's Starlink usage figures as company claims; the new element here is Business Insider's account of the call volume and tasks. BI says Starlink serves more than 6 million active customers.
